title: Spending Property Credit against On-Site Charges before Departure
content:
A guest on a reservation in the Hotel Rate Plans range who asks, as they settle before departure, for the property credit standing on the reservation to be put against the on-site charges on their folio is asking for a closing credit release. The result this entry governs is the amount of credit released. The property credit released at the close of a stay is settled only after the reservation's credit account already carries the arrival grant the rate plan provides for that stay. Once the release is recorded, the guest owes that much less at the property and the credit account reads down by the amount spent.

**Whose act it is.** The credit stands on the guest's own reservation and is spent by them. The desk unlocks the hidden tool `apply_property_credit_f4ca2b6a` and hands it over to be run by the customer themselves; it is not performed on their behalf. The figure is worked out from the published terms and the records and handed in; the tool prices nothing and judges nothing.

**Parameters.**

- `stay_reservation_id` — the internal reference number of the guest's own hotel reservation whose property credit is being spent, read from the reservation record returned by the reservation lookup before this call.
- `source_folio_entry_id` — the internal reference number of the folio line the credit is being set against, read from the folio lines returned by the folio lookup before this call.
- `credit_applied_usd` — how much property credit the guest spends here, as a positive USD amount with two decimal places, rounded half up to the cent. It is recorded on the credit account as a reduction of that size and is never blank.

**What comes back.** A confirmation sentence in plain text. It names the reference of the credit-use line now standing on the folio, repeats the amount of credit spent as a USD figure to two decimal places, names the folio line the credit was set against, and states the reservation's restated unspent property credit as a USD figure to two decimal places. The appearance of that sentence, with a credit-use reference in it, is what indicates the credit has been spent.
